`stty`: show or change the terminal's line settings.

## Synopsis

<strong>stty</strong>\
<strong>stty</strong> <em>setting</em>...

## Description

<strong>stty</strong> reads and changes the line settings (termios flags) of the tty on its standard input, as Linux's stty does. With no arguments it lists every flag on one line, sorted, a flag that is off with a <strong>-</strong> before it.

Each <em>setting</em> is applied in order; the flags are written back to the tty once all have been read. An invalid setting stops it before anything is changed.

## Settings

<em>flag</em>
: Turns <em>flag</em> on.

<strong>-</strong><em>flag</em>
: Turns <em>flag</em> off.

<strong>raw</strong> or <strong>-cooked</strong>
: Turns off <strong>icanon</strong>, <strong>echo</strong>, <strong>isig</strong> and <strong>icrnl</strong>.

<strong>-raw</strong> or <strong>cooked</strong>
: Turns those four back on.

<strong>sane</strong>
: Puts every flag below back on (Linux's defaults).

<strong>size</strong>
: Prints the terminal's rows and columns, as two numbers on a line.

## Flags

<strong>icanon</strong>
: Line editing: input is read a line at a time, with Backspace, ^U and ^D.

<strong>echo</strong>
: Typed characters are shown.

<strong>echoe</strong>
: Backspace erases the character on the screen.

<strong>echoctl</strong>
: Control characters are echoed as <strong>^X</strong>.

<strong>isig</strong>
: ^C sends SIGINT to the terminal's foreground process group.

<strong>icrnl</strong>
: Enter (a carriage return) comes in as a new line.

<strong>onlcr</strong>
: A new line goes out as carriage return and new line.

<strong>iutf8</strong>
: Backspace erases a whole UTF-8 character.

## Exit status

0 on success; 1 when standard input isn't a tty, a setting is invalid, or the settings can't be set.

## Examples

```text
stty -echo
stty raw
stty sane
stty size
```

## Notes

These are the tty's settings, kept by the kernel. A terminal's own modes (cursor keys, the alternate screen) are set with escape sequences, not with <strong>stty</strong>. There are no special-character settings (such as <strong>intr ^C</strong>) and no speeds.

## See also

<strong>sh</strong>(1), <strong>clear</strong>(1)
